_comment: The acceptance matrix for the policy model. `make seed` runs every row and
refuses to report success if any answer differs from `expect`.
Day 3 asks INF to verify relationship queries by hand in the playground. This
file is that verification written down, so it runs on every seed and in CI
rather than living in someone's memory of an afternoon.
The negatives matter more than the positives. A model that says yes correctly
and never says no is not an authorization model.

checks.why: No direct tuple. viewer from parent -> account.viewer -> `[user] or owner`, and Priya owns Northwind. Two hops, zero roles.
Write authority, inherited via `owner from parent`.

The note the demo agent writes its reconciliation summary to.
Contoso's opportunity. No path from Priya, so no access. This is the section 10.1 step 6 denial.
The account itself. Backs the handbook's documented Invariant 1 rejection message.
viewer inherits the parent's viewer, so a read-only user can read children.

THE ASYMMETRY. editor inherits the parent's OWNER, not its viewer. Being able to read an account does not let you write to things under it - this is the line that stops a read-only analyst delegating write authority.
Same asymmetry, on the type the agent actually writes to.
A Keycloak security-admin holds the kill switch, not the data. Authority in the IdP is not authority over records.
A principal with no tuples at all. Deny by default, with nothing configured to make it so.
